chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man upon whom death was approaching, who freed his slave boy and made a bequest, which was more than one-third. He said: 'The manumission of the slave boy is upheld, and the deficiency is taken from what remains (of the estate for the heirs).'

key_terms.حَضَرَهُ الْمَوْتُ: approaching death / at the point of death

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate if a dying person frees a slave and leaves a bequest exceeding one-third?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifying that manumission (itq) is treated as a debt or immediate transfer of ownership, thus taking precedence over the bequest (wasiyyah). Consequently, if the bequest exceeds the permissible one-third limit, the shortfall is deducted from the heirs' share rather than reducing the slave's freedom, reflecting the juristic principle that freeing a slave is a form of settling a debt to God. This distinction highlights the Shia view that itq is not strictly bound by the one-third cap that limits bequests to non-heirs.
